inlines.v: TO'WARDS, preposition [Latin versus, verto.] 1. In the direction to. He set his face toward the wilderness. Numbers 24:1. 2. With direction to, in a moral sense; with respect to; regarding. His eye shall be evil toward his brother. Deuteronomy 28:1. Herein do I exercise myself to have always a conscience void of offense toward God and toward men. Acts 24:1. Hearing of thy love and faith which thou hast toward the Lord Jesus Christ, and toward all saints. Phile 5. 3. With ideal tendency to. This was the first alarm England received towards any trouble. 4. Nearly. I am towards nine years older since I left you. TO'WARD TO'WARDS, adverb Near; at hand; in a state of preparation. TO'WARD, adjective Ready to do or learn; not forward; apt; as a toward youth.
